title: Sanitize system-role markers and patch Unicode tokenizer gaps for stable pinning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During recent onboarding of two community models, we observed token count and role-boundary mismatches between the tokenization used for performance profile publishing and the runtime tokenization. The root causes are: 1) inconsistent encoding of system/assistant role markers in chat templates (mixed ASCII markers and invisible Unicode separators), and 2) tokenizer edge cases for combining characters and emoji sequences that change token boundaries depending on normalization. These mismatches cause published performance profiles to pick suboptimal batch/kv/cache settings and lead to either elevated latency or cost regressions when the pinned model is served in production.
background: We publish per-model performance profiles during onboarding (seq_len distributions, avg tokens per message, kv cache heatmap) which drive kernel selection and batching policies. The onboarding tokenization pass currently reuses a lightweight tokenizer shim that does not normalize invisible separators or collapse system role markers into canonical delimiters. In addition, our tokenizer backend on some worker images uses NFKC normalization by default while the onboarding host used NFD, producing different subtoken splits for names with diacritics and complex emoji sequences. Similar regressions were seen in ENG-214578 and ENG-172410, but those focused on template fallbacks rather than canonical marker sanitization and Unicode normalization.
problem_statement: Onboarding-generated perf profiles can be invalid when tokenizer normalization differs between the onboarding pipeline and the runtime. Need a deterministic preprocessor and gating that ensures the token counts used to publish profiles match the runtime and that chat templates use canonical, visible role markers before tokenization.
proposal: 1) Introduce a deterministic 'onboard-sanitizer' step that: applies NFKC normalization, collapses invisible Unicode separators, and replaces ad-hoc role markers with canonical ASCII delimiters defined in the chat-template spec; 2) Add a tokenizer smoke-check that runs the runtime tokenizer on a sample of onboarding inputs and asserts token-count parity within configurable tolerance; 3) Add a profile-publish gating rule that blocks publish if parity is not met and surfaces a triage report; 4) Add telemetry that records token-delta histograms and top offending codepoints/emoji sequences for rapid triage.
tradeoffs: Sanitization may slightly change exact user-visible message contents (we only alter invisible separators and role delimiter tokens, not user text). Need legal/UX review in edge cases.
Extra onboarding CPU for normalization and smoke-checks increases onboarding latency by ~6-12s for large sample sets — acceptable given higher confidence in the published profile.
Strict gating could delay onboarding for models with genuine tokenizer divergence; we provide an override/expedited path for platform owners with required risk sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline includes 'onboard-sanitizer' run for all chat-style models by default.
For a seeded test corpus (500 messages with diacritics/emoji/system markers), runtime token-count parity to onboarding tokenization is >= 99.5%.
Profile publish step blocks when average token-delta > 1.0 tokens per 100 tokens and uploads a triage report to the onboarding run.
Telemetry dashboard shows token-delta histogram, top 20 offending codepoints, and link to failing sample messages.
Unit and integration tests covering NFKC normalization, marker collapse, and smoke-checks are added to CI with < 30s additional runtime for the unit suite.
A small canary rollout of the sanitized-onboarding flow is executed for two non-critical community models and monitored for 72 hours with no customer-facing regressions.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Implement onboard-sanitizer library (NFKC normalization + marker map) and unit tests.
Week 2: Add tokenizer smoke-check harness that calls the runtime tokenizer binary/container and computes token-delta metrics.
Week 3: Wire gating logic into profile-publish job, add triage report generator and S3 artifact uploads.
Week 4: Add telemetry (Grafana + backfill for recent onboarding runs) and create alert playbook.
Week 5: Run canary onboarding for two community models, collect telemetry, and iterate on false positives.
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalization cases: accented characters, Korean/Japanese combining marks, emoji ZWJ sequences.
Integration test that runs full onboarding for a small model artifact and compares runtime tokenization to onboarding outputs.
Stress test sampling: run smoke-check on a 10k message synthetic corpus to validate performance and resource usage.
Nightly regression job to run previously onboarded models through the sanitizer and check for token-drift over time.
Manual UX spot-check for messages where invisible separators are removed to confirm no visible degradation.
